word:hebrew:H1004.explanation: Bayith means a house. It can also refer to a household or family, as in “the house of Israel.”

word:hebrew:H1048.explanation: This Hebrew word functions as a place name, rendered “Beth.” It identifies a location rather than describing an action, quality, or person. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both within one verse in Joshua 19:21. Because no further definition or surrounding verse text is available here, its secure ordinary meaning is the proper name itself, while the exact location and significance belong to the context of that passage.

word:hebrew:H1211.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “onions,” referring to the familiar food plant. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Numbers 11:5. Its role is simply to name an item of food, and its exact significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and verse text. The word is therefore specific rather than broad: it identifies onions, not a general category of plants or food.

word:hebrew:H1336.explanation: Bether is the name of a craggy place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H1343.explanation: Gêʼeh means lofty. Figuratively, it can describe someone as arrogant or proud.

word:hebrew:H1394.explanation: This Hebrew word is a proper place name, rendered “Gibeath.” It identifies a location rather than describing an action, quality, or object. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Joshua 18:28, and the surviving English renderings preserve it as “Gibeath.” Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its ordinary function is to name a specific place.

word:hebrew:H1400.explanation: Gᵉbar means man and can also mean certain.

word:hebrew:H1509.explanation: This Hebrew word means “inhabited,” functioning as a descriptive term for a place or land. It indicates that the location has the condition of being inhabited, rather than naming a person or an action. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in Leviticus 16:22. Its precise force in that sentence is understood from the surrounding passage, but its basic lexical sense remains “inhabited.”

word:hebrew:H1552.explanation: Gelilah means a region. It can also refer to a border.

word:hebrew:H1718.explanation: Dâdâh means to walk gently or go softly.

word:hebrew:H1754.explanation: Dur means a circle or ball, describing something round in form.

word:hebrew:H1783.explanation: Dinah is a personal name, referring to a woman in the Genesis account. The name appears eight times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all in Genesis. Its first appearance is in Genesis 30:21, and later occurrences identify Dinah in genealogical records and in events involving her family. Because this word functions as a name rather than a general description, its meaning is primarily the identification of this individual. It is rendered “Dinah,” including the possessive “Dinah’s” in one occurrence.

word:hebrew:H1831.explanation: Dema means a tear. It can also figuratively refer to juice or liquor.

word:hebrew:H1897.explanation: Haga means to murmur or mutter, whether by speaking aloud or pondering inwardly.

word:hebrew:H1923.explanation: Hadar means magnificence, and can describe honor or majesty.

word:hebrew:H1956.explanation: Hothir is a Hebrew personal name, rendered as “Hothir.” It does not have an explicit descriptive definition in the available lexical information. The name occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in 1 Chronicles 25:4 and 25:28. Thus, its ordinary function is to identify a person rather than express an action, quality, or object. Its precise significance in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself is preserved as the name Hothir.

word:hebrew:H2016.explanation: Hephek means the reverse, something contrary.

word:hebrew:H2063.explanation: Zoth means “this,” pointing to a thing or matter being identified. It can also mean “hereby,” marking how something is known.

policy.priorReviewerNotes: W1 supports brightness and W3 supports countenance, but Dan 5:6 depicts a troubled, changed countenance and does not directly support the asserted cheerful appearance. The claim therefore combines lexically related senses without valid Scripture support for the exact statement.

word:hebrew:H2179.explanation: This Hebrew word means “hindmost,” identifying what is at the back or trailing end. It functions as a positional term, drawing attention to the last or rear part of something rather than its front or leading part. It occurs twice in the Old Testament, once in Deuteronomy and once in Joshua. Its precise force in either verse depends on the surrounding sentence, but its central idea is the hindmost position.

word:hebrew:H2225.explanation: Zerach means a rising of light, or a rising.

word:hebrew:H223.explanation: Urijah is a personal name, rendered in English as Uriah.

word:hebrew:H2320.explanation: Chodesh means the new moon. It can also mean a month, as shown by references to the second month.

word:hebrew:H2441.explanation: Chek means the palate or roof of the mouth, and it can also refer to the mouth itself. It can also refer to the organ of taste.

word:hebrew:H256.explanation: Ahab is the name of a king of Israel.

word:hebrew:H2575.explanation: Hammath is a Hebrew proper name, rendered “Hammath,” referring to a named location or settlement in the Old Testament. It appears twice in the Hebrew Bible, once in Joshua 19:35 and once in 1 Chronicles 2:55. Because this word functions as a name rather than a description or action, its basic meaning is the identification of Hammath itself; the surrounding verse is needed to clarify its particular role in each passage.

word:hebrew:H2724.explanation: Charabah means a desert. It can also describe dry land or ground.

word:hebrew:H2768.explanation: Chermon is the name of Mount Hermon, a mountain in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H2786.explanation: Charaq means to grate the teeth, or gnash them.

word:hebrew:H2913.explanation: Tachanah means a hand mill. It can also refer to grinding.

word:hebrew:H2966.explanation: Tereph means prey, or something torn by animals. It can describe flesh torn in pieces, distinct from what dies by itself.

word:hebrew:H3091.explanation: Jehoshua is the personal name rendered Joshua in English for the Jewish leader named in Scripture.

word:hebrew:H3158.explanation: Yizreeli means a Jezreelite, or a native of Jezreel.

word:hebrew:H3240.explanation: Yanach means to deposit or put something in a place. It can also mean to leave nations remaining.

word:hebrew:H3305.explanation: Japho is a place in Palestine, also rendered Joppa in English.

word:hebrew:H331.explanation: Atam means to close or shut, including closing the lips or ears. It can also describe something narrow, as with windows.

word:hebrew:H3392.explanation: Jerah is a personal name. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it identifies a person listed in genealogical records, rather than describing an action, quality, or object. The name appears twice, in Genesis 10:26 and 1 Chronicles 1:20, and both occurrences are rendered “Jerah.” Its placement in birth and family-line records shows that it functions as an individual’s name within those genealogies.

word:hebrew:H3433.explanation: This word is a Hebrew personal name, יָשֻׁבִי לֶחֶם, rather than a common noun or ordinary action word. It occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in 1 Chronicles 4:22. The available information identifies the name and its location but does not provide a separate lexical definition or enough surrounding verse text to explain its name meaning more precisely. Its role is therefore best understood as identifying a person in the genealogy or historical record where it appears.

word:hebrew:H3446.explanation: Yischâq is the personal name Isaac.

word:hebrew:H3510.explanation: Ka'ab means to feel pain or grieve. It can also mean to spoil or mar something.

word:hebrew:H3680.explanation: Kasah means to cover something. It can also mean to conceal something, as when transgressions are hidden.

word:hebrew:H3701.explanation: Keçeph means silver. It can also mean money.

word:hebrew:H3860.explanation: Lahen means “therefore,” marking what follows as a consequence.

word:hebrew:H3965.explanation: Maabus means a granary or storehouse.

word:hebrew:H397.explanation: Akish is the name of a Philistine king, rendered Achish in English.

word:hebrew:H4010.explanation: Mablîygîyth means desistance, or rather desolation, and is rendered as comforting oneself against sorrow.

word:hebrew:H4133.explanation: Môtâh means a pole or yoke. It may refer to poles used to carry the ark or yokes put on the neck.

word:hebrew:H4380.explanation: Mekera means a sword. It can also mean a habitation, as in “habitations.”

word:hebrew:H4414.explanation: Mâlach means to salt or season. It can also describe something vanishing away.

word:hebrew:H4458.explanation: Meltachah means a wardrobe—a room where clothing is spread.

word:hebrew:H4537.explanation: Masak means to mix, especially wine with spices.

word:hebrew:H4591.explanation: Ma'at describes becoming small or few. It can also mean making something small or few, or lessening or diminishing it.

word:hebrew:H4605.explanation: Maʻal means upward or above, marking a position higher than something else.

word:hebrew:H4692.explanation: Matsowr means a siege. It can also refer to a fortress or fortified place.

word:hebrew:H4740.explanation: Maqtsowa means an angle or corner. It can also describe a turning in a wall.

word:hebrew:H4832.explanation: Marpe means a remedy, cure, or healing. It can also describe something sound or wholesome.

word:hebrew:H4869.explanation: Misgab is a name for a high refuge or stronghold.

word:hebrew:H50.explanation: Abishua is a personal name referring to a specific man in the Hebrew Old Testament. It functions as a proper name rather than a general description or action word. The name appears five times, all in genealogical lists in 1 Chronicles and Ezra, where Abishua is connected with successive generations and family descent. Its use identifies an individual within Israel’s recorded lineage, especially in priestly genealogy. word:hebrew:H5008.explanation: Na'aq means to groan. It can describe the groaning of someone mortally wounded.

word:hebrew:H5044.explanation: Nibshan is a Hebrew place name, referring to a specific location rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Joshua 15:62, and is rendered as the proper name “Nibshan.” Because it functions as a name, its meaning is primarily identification: it distinguishes one location from other places named in the surrounding geographical record.

word:hebrew:H5093.explanation: Nihyah means lamentation. It can also describe something doleful.

word:hebrew:H5145.explanation: Nezer means something set apart or dedicated; it can also refer to a crown.

word:hebrew:H515.explanation: Eltekon is a proper name, functioning as the name of a particular place rather than describing an action, quality, or object in general. It appears in English as “Eltekon,” so its meaning here is chiefly its identifying use as a place-name, not a translated descriptive term. This Hebrew word occurs once, in Joshua 15:59. The surrounding verse text is needed to explain how the name functions in that specific passage.

word:hebrew:H5189.explanation: Netishah means a tendril or offshoot. It can also refer to branches or plants.

word:hebrew:H5251.explanation: Nes means a flag or banner. It can also mean a pole, as when the bronze serpent was set on one.

word:hebrew:H5303.explanation: Nephilim describes a bully or tyrant. It can also refer to giants.

word:hebrew:H5376.explanation: Nesa means to carry away, to take, or to make insurrection.

word:hebrew:H5398.explanation: Nashaph means to blow, as wind does.

word:hebrew:H5426.explanation: Nethar means to shake off, as leaves are shaken from a tree.

word:hebrew:H5453.explanation: Sibrajim is the name of a place in Syria.

word:hebrew:H5484.explanation: Susah means a mare. It can also refer to a company of horses.

word:hebrew:H5619.explanation: Saqal means to stone—throwing stones at a person or animal.

word:hebrew:H5642.explanation: Sethar means to conceal or keep something secret. In a figurative sense, it can mean to demolish or destroy.

word:hebrew:H5707.explanation: ʻÊd means a witness; it can also mean testimony.

word:hebrew:H582.explanation: Enosh means a mortal human being. It can also refer to a man in general.

word:hebrew:H5835.explanation: Azarah means an enclosure or court. It can also refer to a settle, including the settle of an altar.

word:hebrew:H5927.explanation: ʻAlah means to ascend or go up. It can describe mist going up from the earth, and it can also mean causing frogs to come up onto the land.

word:hebrew:H5981.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “Ummah,” a place name mentioned once in the Old Testament, in Joshua 19:30. It functions as a proper name rather than as a common word describing an action, quality, or object. Because it appears only in this single reference and no verse text or broader lexical definition is available here, the safest understanding is simply the name Ummah. Its precise significance in that passage depends on the surrounding biblical context.

word:hebrew:H6023.explanation: Amashai is a personal name, identifying an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or object. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, in Nehemiah 11:13, and is rendered “Amashai.” Because the available information identifies the name but does not provide a separate definition, its ordinary significance is its role as a person’s name. The surrounding passage is needed to explain who this individual was or what he did there.

word:hebrew:H6056.explanation: Anaph means a bough or branch.

word:hebrew:H6131.explanation: ʻAqar means to pluck up, especially by the roots, and can also describe hamstringing horses.

word:hebrew:H6197.explanation: Eran is a Hebrew personal name, referring to a particular person rather than describing an action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament and is rendered as “Eran.” The available record identifies its single occurrence in Numbers 26:36, but the surrounding verse text is not included here, so no further contextual meaning should be attached to the name. Its normal function is simply to identify the individual named Eran.

word:hebrew:H6229.explanation: Asaq means to press upon—to quarrel or strive with someone.

word:hebrew:H6272.explanation: ʻÂtham probably means to glow. Figuratively, it can describe being desolated; here it is rendered “darkened.”

word:hebrew:H6470.explanation: Pa'am means to impel or agitate—to move or trouble.

word:hebrew:H6557.explanation: Perets is a personal name, appearing in English as Perez or Pharez. Scripture lists Perez among Judah’s sons.

word:hebrew:H6661.explanation: Ziddim is a proper name preserved as “Ziddim,” rather than a Hebrew word translated into an ordinary descriptive term. It identifies a named location in Joshua 19:35. This name appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, so its normal lexical use is simply as a place designation, not as a description of a quality, action, or teaching. The surrounding verse is needed to explain the location’s specific role in that passage.

word:hebrew:H670.explanation: Apharsay means an Apherasite, an inhabitant of an unknown region of Assyria.

word:hebrew:H6904.explanation: This word refers to “war,” describing armed conflict or battle. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Ezekiel 26:9. Because no verse text is provided here, its precise force in that sentence must be understood from the surrounding passage. Its role as the object of related actions indicates that war is presented as something directed, brought, or applied against a target rather than as a person or place.

word:hebrew:H7132.explanation: Qerabah means approaching or drawing near.

word:hebrew:H7169.explanation: Qarats means to wink. It can also describe forming something from clay.

word:hebrew:H7378.explanation: Riyb means to grapple or contend, especially by wrangling in a dispute.

word:hebrew:H7396.explanation: Rikbah means a chariot collectively, or chariots.

word:hebrew:H7460.explanation: Raad means to shudder or tremble.

word:hebrew:H7565.explanation: Resheph means a live coal. It can also describe a spark, burning heat, or a hot thunderbolt.

word:hebrew:H7639.explanation: Sebakah means a network or lattice. It can describe patterned networked work covering the capitals of pillars.

word:hebrew:H7662.explanation: Shᵉbaq means to leave something or let it remain.

word:hebrew:H7767.explanation: Shunammite means a female inhabitant of Shunem. Abishag is called a Shunammite.

word:hebrew:H7833.explanation: Shachaq means to beat something until it is very small or to wear it down.

word:hebrew:H7846.explanation: Set means a departure from what is right, or sin. It can also describe revolters who turn aside.

word:hebrew:H8124.explanation: Shimshai is the personal name of a Samaritan.

word:hebrew:H8168.explanation: Shōal means the palm or hollow of the hand. It can also mean a handful.

word:hebrew:H8186.explanation: Shaʻărûwrâh means something fearful or horrible.

word:hebrew:H8241.explanation: Shetseph means an outburst of anger. It can also mean little.

word:hebrew:H836.explanation: Asher is a personal name and the name of a tribe. It also names a place.

word:hebrew:H8375.explanation: This Hebrew word means “longing,” expressing an intense inner desire for something. It functions as a term that describes what a person feels inwardly, rather than an outward action. In its only recorded Old Testament occurrence, it is rendered “longing” in Psalm 119:20. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself centers on deeply felt desire. word:hebrew:H8425.explanation: Togarmah is the name of a son of Gomer.

word:hebrew:H843.explanation: This Hebrew word is a plural people-group name: “Asherites.” It refers to people identified by that group name rather than describing an action, quality, or object. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Judges 1:32. Because the word occurs only there and the surrounding verse text is not included here, its safest ordinary meaning remains the group designation itself. In a sentence, it functions as a name for a collective people.

word:hebrew:H8520.explanation: Telach is the name of an Israelite. English translations render the name Telah.

word:hebrew:H8663.explanation: Teshuah means a crashing or loud clamor. It can refer to noise, crying, or shouts.

word:hebrew:H894.explanation: Babel is the name rendered as Babylon. It can also refer to Babylonia or the Babylonian empire.

word:hebrew:H911.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to Bedad, a personal name rather than a general description or action. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Genesis 36:35 and 1 Chronicles 1:46, and is rendered “Bedad” in both English renderings. The available scriptural connections place the word as an object in death-related statements, but the precise role of the name in either verse depends on the surrounding passage.
